newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian companies need self-promotion - bourse.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian companies need self-promotion - bourse.

text.p: Lithuanian companies need to promote themselves in a more vigorous manner if they wish to attract badly needed investments and capital, a conference on capital markets was told on Friday.
"Lithuanian companies do not know how to present themselves," Rimantas Busila, the director general of Lithuania's bourse, told reporters at the conference.
Busila's statement was echoed by other officials.
"We have to be more aggressive in presenting ourselves to the world," Arturas Keleras, the president of the country's central depository, said.
"I don't think that enough is being done to promote Lithuania's image abroad," he said.
"Our accounting is Soviet-based...international standards are required of banks but not companies," Eduardas Vilkelis, the heaf of the Association of Lithuanian Banbks, said.
"When foreign investors come, they often do not understand the balance sheets," he said.
Foreign investment is one key area where Lithuania has been viewed as lagging behind its Baltic neighbours Latvia and Estonia.
But analysts say the country, with its larger population and broad range of companies, has more investment potential than its neighbours.
The country's right-of-centre government, brought to power in last autumn's elections, has committed itself to attracting higher levels of foreign investment by speeding up the pace of privatisation.
